authorityBasis: Independent review of this bundle's input and UID-free ACTIVE vocabulary and polynomial boundary authority only.
activeTemplatePolicy: No exact ACTIVE templateKey in the supplied vocabulary matches these H1 polynomial procedures; adjacent or cross-domain patterns are not semantic equivalents.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Write the division identity with quotient and remainder constrained equal to a common polynomial H; apply deg(remainder)<deg(divisor) and degree/leading-coefficient information to determine the possible form of H; use the additional root or divisibility conditions to determine parameters and the requested roots or value.
clusters.variationPolicy: The divisor may be fixed or parameterized and the extra root condition may differ; those condition forms vary while the equal-quotient/remainder degree-bound strategy remains shared.
clusters.noSeparateRule: One L4 can cover equal quotient/remainder conditions when the same degree-bound parameterization and follow-up root filtering are used.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Translate polynomial divisibility into values at its linear-factor roots and branch conditions into alternative point values; enumerate all compatible value triples for the stated degree, construct every nondegenerate polynomial, then aggregate the requested values through a final remainder evaluation.
clusters.variationPolicy: The finite point-value choices and resulting quadratic coefficients vary; the exhaustive case enumeration and aggregation skeleton stays fixed.
clusters.noSeparateRule: This exhaustive family-enumeration procedure is a distinct L4 candidate.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Evaluate a real sum-of-squares identity at a point where its other side vanishes to locate roots of the monic quadratic; substitute the quadratic to determine the dividend; divide by a shifted quadratic divisor and evaluate its degree-bounded remainder at the requested point.
clusters.variationPolicy: The shift, evaluation point, and target point are numerical inputs; the root recovery, substitution and division chain is unchanged.
clusters.noSeparateRule: Keep the sum-of-squares root recovery followed by shifted-divisor remainder calculation as one reusable L4.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Parameterize the linear polynomial; derive the target polynomial from the given identity; reduce it modulo an irreducible quadratic and impose any linear factor condition; solve the resulting coefficient equations, use sign inequalities to select the admissible parameter branch, then evaluate the requested expression.
clusters.variationPolicy: The irreducible quadratic, coefficients, factor root, inequalities, and final expression vary parametrically.
clusters.noSeparateRule: The interaction of quadratic remainder reduction with sign-based branch selection is a distinct L4 candidate.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: For a polynomial divisible by a repeated quadratic factor, parameterize the degree-bounded quotient with the forced leading coefficient; expand the product and compare coefficients to recover the polynomial parameters and quotient, then evaluate the requested scalar.
clusters.variationPolicy: The repeated root and coefficient values change without changing the quotient parameterization and coefficient comparison.
clusters.noSeparateRule: This repeated-divisor coefficient-comparison chain is a distinct L4 candidate.

clusters.repeatableSkeleton: Expand a known quotient–remainder identity for the first divisor; divide the resulting polynomial by a second linear divisor; evaluate the second quotient at the requested point and the second remainder at its divisor root, then combine the values.
clusters.variationPolicy: The initial quotient/remainder and second linear divisor vary; the successive division and two-value combination stay fixed.
clusters.noSeparateRule: A known first division followed by a second quotient/remainder computation is one repeatable chain.

clusters.variationPolicy: The divisor root, multiplier value, and given remainder are direct numerical inputs.
clusters.noSeparateRule: A one-step substitution into a linear-divisor remainder condition is fully covered by the primary remainder theorem and does not warrant an independent L4.
